body.target_estimand: \(\tau=(\tau_D,\tau_S)^\top=\sum_{(d,q)\in\mathcal D\times\mathcal Q}c_{dq}\mu_{dq}\), the fixed finite-population sustained-exposure contrast for each admissible finite \(G\) and \(B\)
body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau=\sum_{d,q}c_{dq}(GBn)^{-1}\sum_{b,g,i}I_{gbi,dq}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{g,2b,i}/\pi_{gbi,dq}\), with \(\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)\Rightarrow N_2(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})\) along every sequence in the structural class \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) for which \(B\to\infty\), \(B^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\), and \(\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})>0\), while the admissible even \(G\) may remain fixed or vary arbitrarily with \(B\)

sampling_model.design: At each block, condition on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), softly tilt the uniform fixed-half saturation assignment by \(f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)\), then randomize fixed treatment counts independently within groups and hold both stages fixed for two periods.  This assignment mechanism is part of the structural design class; covariance-limit conditions enter only the theorems that use them.
sampling_model.units: The finite population consists of \(G\) mutually isolated groups of common size \(n\), observed at the endpoints of \(B\) two-period blocks; potential outcomes are fixed.  The inference regime sends \(B\to\infty\) with even \(G\) fixed or varying arbitrarily, while the projection comparison separately sends \(G\to\infty\).
sampling_model.treatment: The first stage assigns exactly \(G/2\) groups to each of \(q_L=1/4\) and \(q_H=3/4\); the second stage treats exactly \(nq\) units within a group assigned saturation \(q\).
sampling_model.overlap: Complement symmetry gives conditional first-stage probability \(1/2\), so every exposure cell has conditional probability \(p_{dq}/2\geq1/8\).  Feasible pair probabilities are logged, and impossible pairs receive an observable positive-semidefinite completion.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated.  The randomizer records exact conditional first- and second-order inclusion probabilities, and the analysis uses only observed exposure-cell outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 characterize a fixed minimax two-stage spillover-and-carryover design, and the later inference results establish Horvitz--Thompson asymptotics under that design.
Theorems 1--2 give finite-population IPW unbiasedness and a martingale central limit theorem under general adaptive logged assignment probabilities, including sequential rerandomization.
Theorem 1 decomposes the static hard-rerandomization ATE limit into an unaffected Gaussian residual and a truncated Gaussian covariate projection.
Theorems 1--3 provide unbiased joint two-stage effect estimators and conservative randomization covariance formulas under a static design.
The paper derives Berry--Esseen bounds for linear and quadratic functions of standardized permutation estimators.
The paper gives Stein-coupling Berry--Esseen bounds for heterogeneous stratified linear permutation statistics.
The paper establishes asymptotic inference for static two-stage covariate-adaptive randomization under partial interference.
The paper gives broad two-stage interference estimators, central limit theorems, and conservative variance procedures without requiring exposure mappings.
The paper develops exact and asymptotically valid randomization tests for static randomized saturation designs.
The paper constructs Gaussian-prepivoted tests that are exact under sharp nulls and asymptotically valid under weak nulls, including static rerandomized designs.

body.tldr: Predictable soft rerandomization balances lagged group outcomes while preserving the fixed sustained direct-and-spillover target.  The bounded lag-one partial-interference class contains only structural and design-regularity conditions.  On this class, complement symmetry gives exact first-order propensities, score splitting isolates the balanced-sign component, and singular-support Gaussian transport is uniform without covariance-limit assumptions.  Many-block joint inference separately requires rerandomization covariance stabilization and a positive-definite limit, whereas the projection identity \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P\) is a distinct \(G\to\infty\) result requiring the complete-randomization, rerandomization, and projection stabilizations but not positive definiteness.  Logged pair probabilities and a positive-semidefinite completion yield an observable conservative \(2\)-by-\(2\) studentizer and simultaneous Wald coverage.

project_justification.gap: Existing papers separately cover static spillover-and-carryover designs, sequential balance, adaptive martingale inference, and static rerandomization projection geometry.  They do not provide the history-uniform soft-tilt quadratic-moment transport that joins fixed-half group saturations to a joint direct-and-spillover score, nor the resulting separation between arbitrary-\(G\), many-block inference conditions and the \(G\to\infty\) projection conditions.
project_justification.niche: A predictable complement-symmetric kernel preserves exact joint Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness while allowing prior outcomes to guide balance.  Structural membership is kept separate from covariance stabilization, so the same bounded design class supports both fixed-\(G\) many-block inference and growing-\(G\) efficiency analysis under their own explicit hypotheses.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact unbiasedness, a two-stage martingale central limit theorem under separately stated rerandomization covariance conditions, an observable positive-semidefinite-conservative matrix studentizer, simultaneous coverage, a structural-class uniform singular Gaussian transport theorem, and a growing-\(G\) projection covariance identity under exactly the three required stabilization conditions.

body.related_work: Hudgens--Halloran (2008) and Jiang--Imai--Malani (2023) define and estimate direct and spillover contrasts under static two-stage partial interference.  Bojinov--Rambachan--Shephard (2021) supplies the ordinary no-future-assignment nonanticipation convention for dynamic potential outcomes; the stronger lag-one finite-memory equality used here is an imposed restriction tailored to endpoints after two-period held assignments and is not attributed to that paper.  Bojinov--Simchi-Levi--Zhao (2023) is relevant as repeated-block design-based switchback methodology, but it does not supply the partial-interference fixed-half saturation and fixed-count two-stage score used here.  Yu--Ma--Liu (2025) adds carryover and a minimax timing design, but its first-stage law is fixed rather than predictably reweighted by prior outcomes.  Zhou et al. (2018) optimize sequential covariate balance without spillover or carryover inference.  Li--Zhao (2026) provides general adaptive finite-population IPW and martingale theory, including sequential rerandomization; the present contribution is the design-specific conditional covariance and Lindeberg verification for the fixed-half, fixed-count joint sustained-endpoint score.  Li--Ding--Rubin (2018) and Lu et al. (2023) give static hard-rerandomization projection geometry.  Li--Ding (2017), Shi--Ding (2026), and Tian--Yang--Ding (2025) supply finite-population Gaussian approximation tools, but not radial soft weighting of unbounded score quadratics on singular covariance support.  Cohen--Fogarty (2022) is relevant as an alternative Gaussian-prepivoted route to finite-population calibration, whereas this note delivers a direct conservative completed-Wald region.  Masoero et al. (2024) is relevant for the broader multiple-randomization interference setting, but does not give the repeated outcome-adaptive soft-rerandomization joint-inference result.  Jizhou Liu (2026) covers static two-stage covariate-adaptive inference, while the present design is predictably reweighted by prior outcomes across blocks.  He--Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) covers broad exposure-mapping-agnostic two-stage estimators, central limit theory, and conservative variance procedures, but not the logged-pair PSD completion and simultaneous ellipse for this sustained lag-one target.  Liu--Shaikh--Zhong (2026) covers static saturation randomization tests; these results sharpen the boundary around the outcome-adaptive repeated-block theorem proved here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The structural class does not itself guarantee covariance stabilization or a positive-definite limiting covariance.  The arbitrary-\(G\), \(B\to\infty\) central limit theorem and Wald guarantee therefore apply only on sequences satisfying rerandomization covariance stabilization and positive definiteness.  The projection formula is instead a \(G\to\infty\) approximation and requires complete-randomization, rerandomization, and projection stabilization, though not positive definiteness.  The completed studentizer can be conservative by the nonvanishing average completion, and the population gain matrix \(P\) is not generally observable.  Exact enumeration over \(1{,}536\) assignments at \(G=n=4\) remains a finite diagnostic rather than evidence for either asymptotic regime.
body.honest_scope: The estimand is a sustained two-period endpoint contrast under ordinary nonanticipation and an imposed lag-one finite-memory restriction; contemporaneous and carryover components are not separately identified.  Structural membership requires bounded fixed potential outcomes, partial and stratified interference, nonanticipation, lag-one memory, and a uniform imbalance-variance window.  Many-block inference additionally assumes rerandomization covariance stabilization and \(\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})>0\), but permits fixed or arbitrarily varying even \(G\).  The projection identity instead requires \(G\to\infty\) and exactly the complete-randomization, rerandomization, and projection stabilization conditions; it does not require a positive-definite rerandomization limit.  The matrix \(P\) depends on unobserved potential-outcome scores, so \(c^\top Pc>0\) is a theoretical characterization rather than an observable deployment screen.  The Yu--Ma--Liu market calibration and the Bojinov--Shephard trading experiment are prospective design consumers only; ten historical markets do not validate either asymptotic regime.
